questions.text:
Trace through this algorithm with starting value n = 5 and state the final value of total:

  total = 0
  REPEAT while n > 0
    total = total + n
    n = n - 1

What is the final value of total?
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is 15.

Here's why:
The loop runs while n > 0, adding each value of n to total before decreasing n by 1.
Iterations: n=5 (total=5), n=4 (total=9), n=3 (total=12), n=2 (total=14), n=1 (total=15), n=0 (loop stops).
This algorithm sums the integers from 1 to 5: 1+2+3+4+5 = 15.
Exam tip: When tracing a loop, write out the value of every variable after each iteration.

questions.text: Convert the binary number 10110 to decimal (base 10).
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is 22.

Here's why:
In binary, each digit represents a power of 2 from right to left: 10110 = (1×16) + (0×8) + (1×4) + (1×2) + (0×1) = 16 + 0 + 4 + 2 + 0 = 22.
Exam tip: A common mistake is to read the binary digits in the wrong direction — always start with the rightmost digit as the 1s column.

questions.text: Explain the difference between hardware, system software, and application software. Give one specific example of each, and describe how they work together when you open a document.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for clearly distinguishing the three categories with one valid example for each.

Hardware: physical components you can touch (e.g. CPU, RAM, hard drive, keyboard).

System software: programs that manage the computer's resources and provide a platform for other software (e.g. Windows, macOS, Linux).

Application software: programs that perform tasks for the user (e.g. Microsoft Word, Google Chrome).

1 mark for explaining how they work together: e.g. when you open a Word document, the keyboard/mouse (hardware) sends a signal to the operating system (system software), which then loads Word (application software) into RAM (hardware). Word then uses the OS to fetch the document file from the hard drive.

questions.text:
A website asks you to choose a password. Two suggestions are:

(A) Tropical42 — 10 characters, mixed case and numbers, contains a common word
(B) Tr0pic@lFish42! — 15 characters, mixed case, numbers and symbols, no common dictionary word

Which password is stronger, and which TWO factors make it stronger?
options: (A), because shorter passwords are easier to remember
(B), because it is longer AND uses a wider variety of character types
(A), because it contains a real word that is easy to type
(B), because it contains the year you were born
questions.expectedAnswer: (B), because it is longer AND uses a wider variety of character types
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is (B).

Here's why:
Password strength depends on length and the size of the character set (letters, numbers, symbols, mixed case).
A 15-character password with symbols is exponentially harder to brute-force than a 10-character one with only letters and numbers.
(B) also avoids using a plain dictionary word, which makes it resistant to dictionary attacks.

questions.text:
A student posts a photo of themselves and a friend at school, tagging the school's location, on a public social media account.

Explain TWO different risks this creates for their digital footprint, and for EACH risk suggest ONE thing they could do to reduce it.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for each clearly explained risk paired with a sensible mitigation (2 required).

Possible answers (must include the mitigation, not just the risk):

Privacy/safety: revealing the school location lets strangers identify where they are during school hours, creating a safety risk. Mitigation: turn off location tagging and set the account to private.

Consent of others: posting another person without permission may breach their privacy and damage the friendship. Mitigation: ask the friend before posting, and remove tags they did not consent to.

Permanence/future impact: future employers, universities, or scholarship panels may view old posts. Mitigation: think before posting and audit/clean up old posts regularly.

Reputation/screenshots: even if deleted, others may have screenshotted or shared the post. Mitigation: limit posts to a small, trusted audience.

Digital footprint accumulation: tagged content links them to a wider data trail. Mitigation: review tag settings so the user must approve tags before they appear.

Do not award the second mark unless the student gives a different risk for both points.

questions.text:
In a spreadsheet, cell A1 contains 10, cell A2 contains 20, and cell A3 contains 30. A student types the following formula into cell A4:

=A1+A2*A3

What value will appear in cell A4?
questions.markingGuide:
The correct answer is 610.

Here's why:
Spreadsheet formulas follow standard order of operations (BEDMAS): multiplication is done before addition.
=A1+A2*A3 evaluates as 10 + (20 × 30) = 10 + 600 = 610.
A common mistake is to evaluate left-to-right, which would give (10 + 20) × 30 = 900.
If the student wanted that result they would need brackets: =(A1+A2)*A3.

questions.text:
A student writes a Python program to print the numbers 1 to 5, but the output is wrong:

  count = 1
  while count < 5:
      print(count)
      count = count + 1

The program only prints 1, 2, 3, 4. Explain what the bug is and describe how to fix it.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for correctly identifying the bug: the loop condition uses < (less than), so when count reaches 5 the condition 5 < 5 is FALSE and the loop stops before 5 is printed. This is an off-by-one error.

1 mark for a correct fix: change the condition to <= 5 (count <= 5), OR change the starting/ending values so 5 is included (e.g. while count < 6).

Also accept clear explanations that mention 'off-by-one error' or 'boundary condition'.

Exam tip: Off-by-one errors are one of the most common bugs in loops — always check what happens at the very first and very last iteration.

questions.text:
A local sports club wants a simple website. Describe THREE features the website should have. For each feature you must:
• name the feature
• explain why it is useful for the club
• identify ONE technical consideration (e.g. accessibility, privacy, mobile usability, data storage) the developer would need to think about when building it.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark for each feature that includes ALL three parts (feature + usefulness + technical consideration). 3 features required.

Examples of strong answers:

Home page with location, training times and contact details — useful so new members can quickly find out where and when to turn up. Technical consideration: must be mobile-friendly (responsive design) because most users will visit on a phone.

Fixtures/results page — useful so players and supporters can check upcoming games and team performance. Technical consideration: data needs to be easy to update each week (e.g. stored in a CMS or simple database, not hard-coded into HTML).

Contact / sign-up form — useful because people can register interest without coming in person. Technical consideration: must handle personal data privately (HTTPS, Privacy Act 2020 obligations, secure storage of email addresses).

Photo/video gallery — useful for community spirit. Technical consideration: photos of under-18 members need parental consent before publishing.

Members-only section — useful for sharing private team information. Technical consideration: needs login/authentication so only members can see it.

News/events section — useful so the club can promote tournaments and fundraisers. Technical consideration: must be accessible (alt text on images, readable contrast) so all users can read it.

Do NOT award the mark if the technical consideration is missing, generic ('it should look nice'), or just repeats the usefulness.
